name: Grimes
label: 4AD
lede: Claire Boucher made a Dune concept album on cassette, locked herself in a blacked-out Montreal room with GarageBand to make Visions, and has insisted on producing every part of Grimes herself ever since.

eras.title: A loft in Mile End and a cassette about Dune
eras.text: Boucher came east from Vancouver for McGill and found Montreal's loft scene instead. A friend with a live/work space and a label taught her to make tracks; within three years she'd put out two albums on cassette and been thrown out of school.

years.h: "Grimes" goes up on MySpace
years.p: Boucher picks the name from MySpace's genre menu, listing "grime" three times without knowing what grime was.

years.src: Spin: Burning Down the Loft · The Guardian: Grimes, nine days
years.h: Sebastian Cowan opens Lab Synthèse, and she starts making tracks
years.p: The Mile End live/work loft turns the neighborhood's empty buildings into a scene. Cowan, later her manager and engineer, pushes her to produce her own music.
years.xp:
"The loft scene is the foundation of the music scene," Cowan told Spin. Liquor tickets and police attention forced him to shut Lab Synthèse after two years.

When the loft's co-founder, David Matthew Peet, killed himself in 2008, Boucher told the Guardian, she decided to commit to music: "We could all die, at any time. Why the hell am I wasting my time?"

years.h: A homemade houseboat, Minneapolis to New Orleans, impounded
years.p: Boucher and a friend set off down the Mississippi in a boat they built. Engine trouble and the law end the trip, and Minneapolis impounds the boat.
years.xp: She has said newspaper accounts exaggerated what happened. The trip was later made into an animated video narrated by T Bone Burnett.

years.cap: Grimes at the Lo Pub, Winnipeg, August 2010
years.src: Wikipedia: Grimes · NME: Grimes, On this record
years.h: Geidi Primes, a Dune concept album on cassette
years.p: Released by Cowan's Arbutus Records in Montreal. Halfaxa follows in October.
years.xp: "When I first started everyone was like, 'Ha, ha, a Dune concept album,'" she told NME in 2015. "But now because of Game Of Thrones and stuff it's more chill."

years.cap: Grimes at the Rialto Theatre, Montreal, Pop Montreal, September 2010
years.src: Wikipedia: Grimes · The Guardian: Grimes, nine days
years.h: McGill expels her for skipping classes
years.p: She had started in Russian literature and switched to neuroscience, the Guardian reported, and her parents were mildly horrified when she went full time on Grimes.

eras.title: Nine days without sleep
eras.text: Visions was made in about three weeks in a blacked-out room on GarageBand, and it turned an Arbutus cassette artist into a 4AD act with Pitchfork's song of the year. Courted by fashion houses and blogs at once, Boucher started talking about branding the way other indie acts talked about guitars.

years.cap: D'Eon and Grimes at Pop Montreal
years.src: Wikipedia: Grimes · The Guardian: Grimes, nine days
years.h: Darkbloom: a split 12-inch with d'Eon
years.p: Five songs from Grimes, the rest from d'Eon, on Arbutus and Hippos in Tanks. The cover shows the two dressed as cave-dwellers.

years.h: On tour opening for Lykke Li
years.p: Grimes supports [[Lykke Li|cc7d4686-ea02-45fd-956e-94c1a322558c]] across North America, playing to rooms far bigger than Mile End's lofts.

years.h: Oblivion leaks out ahead of the album
years.p: A promotional release in October 2011. The next year Pitchfork names it the best song of 2012.
years.xp: Emily Kai Bock's video puts Boucher at Montreal's Olympic Stadium during a football game and a motocross rally, deliberately surrounded by men. The song deals with her experience of assault and the fear that followed, and the video was made as a choice to walk back into that kind of space.

years.src: The Guardian: Grimes, nine days · Wikipedia: Grimes
years.h: 4AD signs her, then a whole scene
years.p: After Grimes, 4AD goes back to Montreal for Purity Ring, whose Corin Roddick played in her touring band Born Gold.

years.cap: Grimes live in Austin during SXSW, March 2012
q: Once you hit day nine, you start accessing some really crazy shit
years.src: The Guardian: Grimes, nine days · Wikipedia: Visions
years.h: Visions, made on GarageBand in three weeks
years.p: Arbutus in Canada, 4AD in the US. Pitchfork puts it at No. 6 for the year and it wins the Juno for Electronic Album of the Year.
years.xp:
Boucher recorded it in her Mile End apartment with the windows blacked out, going nine days without sleep or food and taking amphetamines to keep going. "Once you hit day nine, you start accessing some really crazy shit," she told the Guardian.

She also called it "so tortured" underneath, a record about working through drug use, two friends' deaths, an assault and bad relationships: "It can totally be a party album if you want, which is hilarious to me."

years.h: After her hometown show, an Arcade Fire summit on a pool table
years.p: At 4am after a Cabaret du Mile End gig, the Guardian finds her deep in talk with Win Butler and Régine Chassagne of [[Arcade Fire|52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68]].

years.h: The Visions tour reaches Gothenburg
years.p: Two years on the road with Born Gold, Elite Gymnastics and others, ending in 2014.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grimes · NME: Grimes, On this record
years.h: Jay-Z's Roc Nation takes over her management
years.p: Boucher, still on an indie label, signs with Roc Nation management.

eras.title: A song for Rihanna, a scrapped album, every credit hers
eras.text: The follow-up took three years and one thrown-away album. Boucher moved to Los Angeles, taught herself guitar and violin, and made Art Angels without a co-producer, an engineer or a studio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grimes · Wikipedia: Art Angels · NME: Grimes, On this record
years.h: Governors Ball, between albums
years.p: Grimes plays Randall's Island in New York in the middle of a long wait for the follow-up to Visions.
years.xp: She'd retreated to Squamish, north of Vancouver, to write, and scrapped most of what she made there. "I was writing these really depressing songs, and nothing was fun at all," she said. She started over in Los Angeles.

years.h: Go was written for Rihanna. Rihanna said no
years.p: Grimes releases the Blood Diamonds production herself. Some fans call it pandering to radio; Rolling Stone puts it at No. 14 among the year's songs.

years.h: Realiti, a demo she calls a mess, wins everyone over
years.p: Posted as a gift to fans from the scrapped sessions, it's called the best Grimes song since Visions. She re-records it for the album.

years.cap: Grimes on the Art Angels tour, Laneway Festival, Brisbane
q: On this record I don't give a fuck anymore
years.src: NME: Grimes, On this record · Wikipedia: Art Angels
yt: Flesh Without Blood / Life in the Vivid Dream
years.h: Every credit on Art Angels reads Claire Boucher
years.p: Recorded alone in her LA home studio in Ableton, with guests [[Janelle Monáe|ee190f6b-7d98-43ec-b924-da5f8018eca0]] and the Taiwanese rapper Aristophanes. NME names it album of the year.
years.xp:
She'd posted the engineer and producer credits on Instagram as "Fillin out tha paperwork": every line said Claire Boucher. "I'm less afraid of saying things now. I used to be so scared, I was turning the vocals down and drenching them in reverb," she told NME's Kevin EG Perry.

Metacritic averages 88 and Pitchfork ranks it No. 3 of 2015. By 2019 she was calling it "a piece of crap."

years.src: Wikipedia: Grimes · NME: Grimes, On this record
years.h: Grimes takes Art Angels to Lollapalooza
years.p: With Hana alongside her, she tours Asia and Europe as the Ac!d Reign tour and North America as March of the Pugs, then supports Florence and the Machine.
years.xp: The video for Kill V. Maim won the Juno for Video of the Year in 2017. Boucher had told NME she was thinking about hypnosis to deal with stage nerves.

eras.title: The villain, on purpose
eras.text: Collaborations with Janelle Monáe and Hana, a very public relationship with Elon Musk, and an album about a goddess of climate change. Her last record for 4AD leaked half-finished and came out a week before the pandemic shut everything down.

years.h: Venus Fly with Janelle Monáe
years.p: Grimes and [[Janelle Monáe|ee190f6b-7d98-43ec-b924-da5f8018eca0]] trade verses on the Art Angels track's video, which wins Best Dance Video at the Much Music Video Awards. A year later Grimes appears on Monáe's Pynk.

years.h: Two albums promised, one for 4AD
years.p: She says the 4AD record will be collaborative and full of light, the other "pure darkness and chaos" for an unnamed label.

years.h: A pun about Rococo's basilisk leads to Elon Musk
years.p: Grimes and Musk meet after both landing on the same AI joke on Twitter. Their relationship runs, on and off, until around 2021.
years.xp: Their son, X Æ A-Xii, was born in May 2020; a daughter followed via surrogate in 2021 and a third child was reported in 2023. In September 2023 Grimes filed suit in California over parental rights. She has also publicly criticized Musk, including in February 2025 over bringing their son to public events.

years.h: Violence, with the producer i_o
years.p: The first single from the climate-goddess album; her brother Mac Boucher co-produces the video. Seven weeks later, an unfinished version of the whole record leaks online.

years.h: Miss Anthropocene is her last album for 4AD
years.p: A concept record about a goddess of climate change. It gives her a first UK Top 10, at No. 10.
years.xp: Personifying climate change made it "a bit easier to look at" than abstract doom, she said, and the media's casting of her as a villain led her to pursue villainy artistically. Delete Forever was written after Lil Peep's death. In December 2020 she swapped the cover art for a painting by Rupid Leejm.

eras.title: After 4AD, an album still called not quite done
eras.text: Off 4AD, Boucher signed to Columbia, sold digital art, opened her voice to anyone with an AI model and announced album after album. The singles kept coming; the full-length kept moving.

years.h: Columbia Records signs her
years.p: Earlier that year she sold digital art as NFTs for $5.8 million, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Player of Games and a sixth album called Book 1
years.p: Book 1 is announced the same day; Shinigami Eyes follows in January 2022.

years.h: Anyone can use her voice, for half the royalties
years.p: Grimes invites people to make songs with an AI model of her voice and offers to split royalties 50/50.

years.big: "I'm not good enough at math for this shit."
years.h: Coachella: tracks at double speed, live on the stream
years.p: About 20 minutes into her 50-minute DJ set, the music runs at double tempo and Grimes stops to explain over the mic.
years.xp: The set had opened with Grimes pulled on stage in a mechanical spider. The next day she apologized: she'd outsourced the rekordbox BPMs and track organization for the first time, "I had a bad feeling beforehand," and the second weekend would be "flawless, everything will run thru my hand."

years.cap: Grimes DJing in the Sahara tent at Coachella
years.h: Artificial Angels
years.p: A new single, with a video three days later. In April 2026 she starts teasing an album called Psy Opera, which she says is not quite done.
